fieldNotes.location: Roster's geocode (200 Caron Rd / 41.9356,-89.0546) landed on a large white retail/warehouse-type building with no docks or trailer yard — NOT the meat plant. Hormel's own page lists the plant at 1001 S Main St. Resolved the plant to the old rail-served industrial parcel at the Main St rail crossing (~41.9205,-89.0698), confirmed by Street View showing a tall smokestack, water tower, ammonia/refrigeration tanks and rail tank cars — classic markers of an older urban meat-packing plant.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint visible at any access point. The plant is an old, compact, open urban facility hemmed by residential streets and rail; truck access is via the rail-crossing road and an unpaved/gravel lot on the east side (Street View 2022).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Low-confidence — this is a dense multi-building old plant with conveyor bridges between structures; visible dock-door banks are small. Estimated ~8 doors (0-10 band).
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Plant is tightly bounded by active rail lines on both north and south and by residential streets; any truck queue would have very little stacking room and could foul a rail crossing.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur and tank cars confirmed in Street View; the plant sits between two rail lines.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rochelle is a small Ogle County town (~9,000 pop.); the plant sits just outside a two-block downtown surrounded by residential blocks — small-town industrial, classified Rural per rubric.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Multiple connected old structures with overhead conveyor/pipe bridges; counted ~4 distinct buildings, low confidence.
